summary: 9 checks passed, 2 backend test cases failed (both from one root-cause bug: seeded admin/admin123 account does not exist in DB). All other login criteria (operator/viewer login, wrong-credential rejection, case sensitivity for a working account, password toggle, session persistence/logout, unauthenticated redirects, role gating) pass.

checks.criterion: User reported 'cannot login'. Verify login works with the seeded admin account at /login
checks.name: login-admin-dashboard
checks.evidence: UI: submitting admin/admin123 on /login shows error 'Username atau password salah' and stays on /login (console: 401 on POST /api/auth/login). Screenshot: login-admin-dashboard-after-submit.png. Backend cross-check: curl -X POST :8001/api/auth/login {username:admin,password:admin123} -> 401 {"detail":"Username atau password salah"}. DB query on users collection shows NO document with username 'admin' exists (only operator1, viewer1, and an unrelated admin-role user 'dodo'). ensure_default_admin() only bootstraps admin when the users collection is completely empty, so once operator1/viewer1/dodo were seeded, the default admin was never created.

checks.criterion: Login works for the operator and viewer accounts too
checks.name: login-operator-viewer-roles
checks.evidence: operator1/operator123 and viewer1/viewer123 both land on '/' with current-user-name containing 'Operator Gudang' and 'Pemantau Stok' respectively (actual full names are 'Operator Gudang Siang' / 'Pemantau Stok' - briefing's exact-match wording for operator was slightly off vs seed data; not a bug, noted in action_items).

checks.criterion: Wrong or unknown credentials show a clear error and do NOT log the user in
checks.name: login-rejects-wrong-credentials
checks.evidence: user@email.com/whatever123 and operator1/totally-wrong-pw both show 'Username atau password salah' and remain on /login.

checks.criterion: Login works for the operator and viewer accounts too (backend)
checks.name: test_login_success_seeded_accounts
checks.evidence: pytest tests/test_tscheck_login.py::test_login_success_seeded_accounts - parametrized case 'admin-admin123' FAILS: POST /api/auth/login {username:admin,password:admin123} -> 401 (expected 200). operator1 and viewer1 parametrized cases PASS (200, gp_session cookie set, /auth/me returns correct user).

checks.criterion: Unauthenticated requests to protected endpoints are rejected (supports redirect-to-login criterion)
checks.name: test_unauthenticated_requests_rejected

checks.criterion: Login rejects unknown account / wrong password (backend)
checks.name: test_login_rejects_unknown_account / test_login_rejects_wrong_password
checks.evidence: POST /api/auth/login with user@email.com -> 401 'Username atau password salah', no gp_session cookie. POST with admin/wrong-pass-123 -> 401, no cookie.

checks.criterion: Password is case-sensitive but username is not
checks.name: login-username-case-insensitive
checks.evidence: Tested against operator1 (admin unusable due to the bug above): 'Operator1'/operator123 logs in successfully; 'operator1'/'Operator123' (wrong case password) is rejected with the error message and stays on /login.

checks.criterion: Password is case-sensitive but username is not (backend, admin-specific per briefing wording)
checks.name: test_username_case_insensitive_password_case_sensitive
checks.evidence: POST /api/auth/login {username:Admin,password:admin123} -> 401 (expected 200) - same root cause as the missing 'admin' account bug above. The wrong-case-password half of this test (admin/Admin123 -> 401) passes as expected, but is meaningless while the base account itself does not exist.

checks.criterion: Show/hide password toggle on the login form works
checks.name: login-password-toggle-visibility
checks.evidence: login-password-input type toggles password -> text -> password on clicking login-toggle-password twice.

checks.criterion: Session persists across a page reload and logout ends it
checks.name: session-persists-reload-and-logout
checks.evidence: Logged in as operator1 (admin unusable), reload keeps user on '/' with current-user-name intact; logout returns to /login; subsequent direct navigation to '/' redirects to /login.

checks.criterion: Unauthenticated visitors are redirected to the login page
checks.name: unauthenticated-redirects-to-login
checks.evidence: With cookies cleared, navigating to '/', '/products', '/settings' all redirect to /login.

checks.criterion: Role gating still holds after the login changes
checks.name: role-gating-viewer-and-operator
checks.evidence: viewer1: dashboard body text contains no 'Rp<digit>' currency pattern; /settings and /shipments both redirect back to '/'. operator1: nav has zero 'Pengaturan'/'Pengguna' links; /settings redirects back to '/'.

bugs.title: Seeded admin account (admin/admin123) does not exist - reproduces the user's 'cannot login' report
bugs.description: The users collection contains operator1, viewer1, and an unrelated admin-role account named 'dodo', but no document with username 'admin'. lib/auth.py::ensure_default_admin() only inserts the default admin when db.users is completely empty at startup, so once other users were seeded/created, the default admin credentials documented everywhere (memory/test_credentials.md, the briefing, and the login card's own onboarding hint) stopped working. Both the UI (login-admin-dashboard check) and the API (POST /api/auth/login) reproduce this: 401 'Username atau password salah' for admin/admin123 and for Admin/admin123 (case-insensitive username variant).
bugs.evidence: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8001/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}' -> 401 {"detail":"Username atau password salah"}. Direct DB read of db.users shows no username=='admin' document. Browser check login-admin-dashboard screenshot login-admin-dashboard-after-submit.png shows the error banner and URL staying on /login.

action_items.detail: Create/restore the admin/admin123 account (or update documented credentials) so ensure_default_admin's guarantee holds even when other users already exist - e.g. seed_users.py or a startup check should ensure at least one account matching DEFAULT_ADMIN_USER exists, not just 'any user exists'.

Briefing text says operator1's header chip shows exactly 'Operator Gudang', but seed data's full_name is 'Operator Gudang Siang'. Not a bug - just a wording mismatch between briefing and seed data; checks were adjusted to toContainText.
